text:
The Blackhawks' season changed this week. Connor Bedard, the captain, will have surgery on his right shoulder, The Athletic's Scott Powers and Mark Lazerus reported, and Chicago is now planning around a long stretch without him. The same day Lazerus wrote that Rickard Rakell had the Blackhawks on his no-trade list, and asked whether all the losing has made Chicago a place players avoid.

At 7-14-2 there is little to argue with in the record. Chicago has 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and has allowed 4.0 goals a game. The Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov pair has been outscored 15-4 at 5-on-5 with a third of the chances. The goaltending changed too: Arvid Soderblom, who lost his last four starts in Chicago, was traded to the Rangers for Spencer Martin, leaving Spencer Knight as the starter.

The reasons to keep watching are young. Sam Rinzel has 15 points in his last 10 games against 5.7 expected, including the winner in Calgary on Saturday, so expect that pace to cool even if the player is real. Frank Nazar has 9 in 10, and his line with Patrick Kane and Oliver Moore takes 55% of the expected goals, the best of Chicago's regular trios.

Our playoff odds are effectively zero. What we'd watch: how the kids handle the minutes Bedard leaves behind.
